title: SAMPLED REVIEW
rule: the screen is the page, the review is drawn on it, and the margins take the screen's own colour
description: Redline's frame with sampled-ground's palette rule (round-6 N1). Three screens fill the page between two solid margins: Bayyinah TV's live room (2023–26, a recreation), Design System v2 in its Storybook (2026) and the care platform's glucose overview (2026); the last two are real product screens with invented data. Each sheet carries four notes in its margins, each a decision and its result, and each note draws a hairline into the screen and rings the part it is about. The margins and the ground are computed from the screen's measured hue at fixed lightness and chroma, so the frame takes the colour of the screen inside it; when the next sheet becomes current, its colour spreads out of its plate over margins, ground and bar together. A record of ten decisions closes the page on a grey sheet with no hue; its footnote is the only place the colour rule is stated.
signature: Bricolage Grotesque (700 at 64 px for the claim, 450/700 for decision → result titles, 650 for note heads) and Gentrit Technical Mono for ids, captions, chips and results. Palette by construction: margins oklch(0.42 0.13 h) with ground-colour type, ground oklch(0.95 0.035 h), ink oklch(0.30 0.11 h); h = 34 (live room), 230 (Storybook screen), 154 (care screen), chroma 0 for the record (measured hues from sampled-ground's histogram method). First screen: 'Two platform rewrites, three apps in both stores.', one identity line with CV and Email, 'Rebuild Bayyinah TV on Nuxt 3 → 34 routes, 270+ components.', the live room (952 × 442, mounted paused) with four notes and four rings, and the caption '0005 · 2023–26 · Frontend, core team · Recreation, invented data'. The sticky bar holds only the three sheet chips and the record chip. Motion: (1) at arrival, four hairlines draw from the note badges across the margin into the screen (180 ms each, 60 ms stagger, cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)) and each ring lands 160 ms after its line starts (120 ms, opacity and scale 0.96 → 1); (2) when the scroll rests on a new sheet for 160 ms, a clip-path circle spreads its colour from its plate's centre over the fixed frame and the bar (one layer in each, one keyframe set, 280 ms ease-out), so margins, ground and bar arrive by one means; (3) hover or focus a note and the other marks fade to 0.2 in 160 ms, hover a ringed part and its note lights. Chips, record rows and notes jump with no travel and switch the colour at once. Reduced motion: lines and rings appear, the colour switches with no spread, the live room shows its static state and runs no timer, the two screenshots do not move. Phone: no margins; the plate keeps four numbered pins on the same four parts as the desktop and the notes stack under it in a block of the sheet's margin colour.

bundle: Draft chunk about 8 kB gzip JS and 3.3 kB gzip CSS; the recreations are the shared lazy chunks
holdback: Lowest: not overwhelming, 8 (seniority, motion, original and hooks are also 8). The first screen still holds the claim, the identity line, the sheet title, a live room with four rings and four notes, and two dark margins (37.1% chroma, 49.5% outside the plate); it is calmer than redline but it is not a quiet page. Seniority: the notes are decisions with results, but some results restate the product ('Realtime chat, moderated in the same column', 'Each reading shows in the patient's own timezone') because the content has no outcome number for them, and the care title's result is a method ('one route at a time, on Design System v2'). Original stays 8, not 9: an annotated screenshot is a known case-study device and the colour rule comes from sampled-ground; the new part is the combination. The aim of 60 is not reached by my strict count (57). Known limits: plates are 952 px wide, not the 1200 × 540 of the plan, because the notes need 208 px margins; the paused live room leaves the lower third of its chat column empty; the phone live-room plate is 343 × 300, not 258, so the four pins stay on legible parts; on a phone the non-current chips show only their numbers; controls inside the shared recreations (Mute, the theme segment) are under 44 px; the keyboard frame for a note was taken with element.click() (detail 0), because the capture script sends no char event for Enter on a button.
